text: Import images and videos from a directory. Imported files are added to the thumbnail list.

Image options for preprocessing.
Resize Mode: Method to resize images to target resolution.
Resolution: Target resolution for processed images.
Non-square Framing: Enable non-square aspect ratios for processed images.
Aspect Ratio: The ratio between width and height dimensions.
Padding Options: Padding method for non-square images.
Frame rate for extracting frames from video files.\nHigher FPS will extract more frames but take longer.

Applies data augmentation during processing to increase dataset diversity. Use cautiously for orientation-sensitive data.\nX-Flip: Flip images horizontally (left-right).\nY-Flip: Flip images vertically (up-down).

Perform model training on your dataset. Ensure you have prepared a dataset from the data preparation module before training.
Save Path: Model checkpoints and generated images will be saved here during training
Resume Pkl: Model checkpoint file (.pkl) to resume training. Leave empty to start from scratch
Training Augmentation: In-training data augmentation method to improve training stability on smaller datasets. ADA - Adaptive Discriminator Augmentation, DiffAUG - Differential Augmentation
Augmentation Pipeline: Specific configuration of the data augmentation pipeline. Different augmentation methods have different options
Batch Size: Number of images per training batch. Larger batches require more VRAM
Configuration: Model architecture preset. stylegan2 - StyleGAN2, stylegan3-t - StyleGAN3 translation-equivariant, stylegan3-r - StyleGAN3 rotation-equivariant

Advanced settings for fine-grained control over the training process. 
Generator LR: Generator learning rate. Leave blank to use the selected config's default (0.002 for stylegan2, 0.0025 for stylegan3)
Discriminator LR: Discriminator learning rate
Gamma: Training stability parameter
Snapshot: Checkpoint saving interval
Mirror: Dataset flip augmentation. None - no flips, X - horizontal flip, Y - vertical flip, X+Y - all four flip orientations. Do not combine with the X-Flip/Y-Flip options on the Prepare screen.

Project a target image, text prompt, or both to find the closest latent vector of a trained model.
Network Path: Path to the trained StyleGAN2 model (.pkl file)
Target Image: Image to project into the latent space
Target Text: Text description to guide the projection (optional)
Output Directory: Directory to save projection results
Save Video: Save the projection process as a video
Seed: Random seed for reproducibility
Learning Rate: Learning rate for optimization
Steps: Number of optimization steps
Use VGG: Use VGG perceptual loss
Use CLIP: Use CLIP-based semantic guidance
Use Pixel: Use pixel-wise loss
Use Penalty: Apply regularization penalty
Use Center: Center the latent code initialization

Identify and extracts interpretable feature directions in the latent space of a trained model.
Network Path: Path to the trained StyleGAN2 model (.pkl file)
PCA Estimator: PCA estimation method to use (pca/ipca/fbpca/ica/spca)
Features: Number of principal components to extract
Sparsity: Sparsity parameter for sparse PCA
Save Path: Directory to save extracted features

Upscale images and videos for higher resolution.
Save Path: Directory to save enhanced results
Model: Model type. Quality (best quality, slowest), Balance (balanced), Fast (fastest)
Scale Mode: Choose between custom resolution or scale factor
Scale Factor: Scale factor for output resolution
Width: Custom output width in pixels
Height: Custom output height in pixels
Sharpening: Additional sharpening strength (1 = normal, higher = sharper)
Mix two trained models to make a new model.

Resolution Layers: Layer groups by resolution
Model Selection: Select which model's weights to use for each layer
X: Disable layers from this point
Recover: Restore previous layer settings

Controls for the output display and for capturing it.
Raw Scale: Shows the visuals at their native size.
Fit: Scales the visuals to fill the preview area.
Super Resolution: Upscales the generated images in real time.
Fullscreen: Shows the visuals in full screen on the main display.
Screenshot: Saves a snapshot of the visuals as an image in the captures folder.
Record: Records the visuals as a video in the captures folder. Press Stop to finish.
Network & latent settings for controlling the model and latent space

Controls for diversity and noise generation.
Diversity: Controls image variation. 0 produces the same image every time, values around 0.8–1.0 balance diversity and dataset fidelity.
Noise: Toggles noise on or off. Disabling noise results in smoother images with fewer textures.
Global Noise: Adjusts the overall strength of noise applied to the image.
Noise Seed: Sets the noise seed to change texture while keeping the same image structure.
Anim: Animates noise by changing the noise seed every frame.
Settings for creating animation loops

Performance stats and input/output settings.
GUI / Render: Frame time and frame rate of the interface and of image generation.
FPS limit: Caps the interface frame rate, which also limits how often new images are generated.
Vertical sync: Syncs the interface with the display refresh rate.
GPU / CPU: Device used for image generation.
Force FP32: Forces full 32-bit precision, can fix visual artifacts at some performance cost.
OSC input: Source and port Autolume listens on for incoming OSC signals. Any network receives from other devices such as phones and controllers. This machine receives only from this computer. The source list also shows this computer's addresses. Use one of them as the destination in the app sending OSC.
NDI output: Streams the visuals over NDI under the given name when enabled.

Stylizes the live output with an image to image diffusion model.
Enable: starts processing. The checkpoint loads on the first frame, which takes a few seconds; the image keeps playing while it loads.
Prompt: describes the target look. It applies live with no reload, so it is safe to change mid performance. Recent lists prompts you used before.
Strength: how far the image moves from the StyleGAN output. Around 0.4 keeps the original pose and identity and restyles the surface; 0.7 and above repaints the frame.
Seed: fixes the diffusion noise, so the same settings reproduce the same frame.
Checkpoint: a Hugging Face model id, or a file in the diffusion/checkpoints folder of your data folder.
Resolution: the size the diffusion runs at. Higher is sharper and slower; 512 is what these models were trained on.
LoRA: an optional style adapter. It must match the checkpoint architecture, and a mismatch silently does nothing. Unticking keeps the file and weight for later.
Weight: how strongly the LoRA applies. Around 1 suits most style LoRAs; slider LoRAs work beyond that and can go negative.
TensorRT: runs through compiled engines, 2 to 3 times faster. Each combination of checkpoint, LoRA, weight and resolution needs its own 20 to 30 minute build.
Changing anything under Model setup reloads the pipeline, which takes a few seconds.
